answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks via flow-capped trust graphs rooted at audited seeds. Peers stake forfeitable collateral on links, and routers cap any cluster's tasks, like translating a fable or tagging a meadow, at the min-cut capacity of paths that bridge it to the core. Because scaling throughput requires independent, collateralized endorsements per identity, unbacked accounts yield no extra revenue. However, honest newcomers in sparse clusters face cold-start exclusion.
